# flow

orchestrate many coder tasks from one TypeScript file

Orchestrate many coder tasks with a plain TypeScript file: dispatch, gates,
concurrency, journaling, and resume. Flows live in .coder/flows/ (workspace)
or ~/.coder/flows/ (global). See `coder docs flows`.

## `flow run <flow> [inputs] [--wait] [--args <args>] [--concurrency <concurrency>] [--max-tasks <max-tasks>] [--dry-run] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

run a flow in the background (--wait to follow it live)

Run a flow: a TypeScript file that orchestrates many coder tasks with gates,
journaling, and resume. Prints the run id and orchestrates in the background;
--wait follows the run in the foreground with live progress (Ctrl-C detaches;
it keeps running), and `coder flow watch` shows the same lines any time.
Stop a run with `coder flow stop`.

- `<flow>` the flow: a discovered name or a path
- `<inputs>` the flow's input as bare key=value pairs
- `--wait` follow the run in the foreground (Ctrl-C detaches; it keeps running)
- `--args <args>` the flow's input as a JSON value (or pass bare key=value pairs)
- `--concurrency <concurrency>` tasks running at once (default: CPU count)
- `--max-tasks <max-tasks>` total tasks the run may dispatch (default: CPU count x 10)
- `--dry-run` print every resolved prompt and gate command without dispatching
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

```sh
coder flow run audit-routes --wait  # run a discovered flow
coder flow run ./scratch/one-off.ts --wait  # run a flow by path
coder flow run verify --args '{"clusters":["a","b"]}' --wait  # pass structured input
```

## `flow list [--archived] [--limit <limit>] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

recent flow runs (by default running + just stopped)

List recent flow runs, most recent first: running runs plus ones that ended
within the last 30 minutes. Older runs auto-archive and move to --archived.

- `--archived` show archived runs (auto-archived or via flow archive)
- `--limit <limit>` show at most n runs (default all)
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

## `flow discover [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

list flows runnable here (workspace + global)

List every flow discoverable from the current directory: workspace flows in
.coder/flows/ (walking up to the repo root) and global flows in ~/.coder/flows/.

- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

## `flow result [run-id] [--tail <tail>] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

progress and result of a run

Show a flow run's status and result, with its tasks, gates, and token ledger.
--tail <n> caps the step rows (0 for the result alone). Defaults to the most
recent run. To watch a run live, prefer `coder flow watch`.

- `<run-id>` the run (default: the most recent)
- `--tail <tail>` show the last n step rows (default: all; 0 hides them)
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

```sh
coder flow result --tail 0  # the most recent run's result, no step rows
```

## `flow watch [run-id] [--tail <tail>] [--from <from>] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

watch a run live (replay + follow)

Watch a flow run live: replay its progress lines from the start, then keep
following while it runs (Ctrl-C detaches; it keeps running). Blocks until it
finishes; exits 0 on success, 1 otherwise. Defaults to the most recent run.
For the result alone, prefer `coder flow result`. Alias: stream.

With --from <n>, or as a tool, it returns the events from event n on without
following, and `next`: the command that continues them while the run goes on.

- `<run-id>` the run (default: the most recent)
- `--tail <tail>` replay only the last n events first (default: all)
- `--from <from>` return the events from event n on instead of following them
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

```sh
coder flow watch  # follow the most recent run to completion
coder flow watch <run-id> --from 0 --json  # the events so far, and the command that continues them
```

## `flow stop [run-id] [--keep-tasks] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

stop a run and its still-running tasks

Stop a running flow: signal the orchestrator so it stops dispatching, stamp the
run stopped, and stop its still-running tasks. Defaults to the most recent run;
the journal stays ready for `coder flow resume`.

- `<run-id>` the run (default: the most recent)
- `--keep-tasks` leave the run's still-running tasks running
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

## `flow resume [run-id] [--wait] [--args <args>] [--concurrency <concurrency>] [--max-tasks <max-tasks>] [--dry-run] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

continue a stopped or edited run

Re-run a flow from its journal: finished steps replay instantly, the first
changed or new step onward runs live. Defaults to the most recent run.
Accepts the same flags as flow run.

- `<run-id>` the run (default: the most recent)
- `--wait` follow the run in the foreground (Ctrl-C detaches; it keeps running)
- `--args <args>` the flow's input as a JSON value (or pass bare key=value pairs)
- `--concurrency <concurrency>` tasks running at once (default: CPU count)
- `--max-tasks <max-tasks>` total tasks the run may dispatch (default: CPU count x 10)
- `--dry-run` print every resolved prompt and gate command without dispatching
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

```sh
coder flow resume  # continue the most recent run
```

## `flow archive [run-id] [--all-stopped] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

hide a run (or all stopped) from the list

Archive a flow run so it drops out of the default list (see it again with
`coder flow list --archived [--limit N]`). Pass --all-stopped to archive every
finished run. A running run must be stopped first.

- `<run-id>` the run to archive
- `--all-stopped` archive every stopped (finished) run
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)

## `flow delete [run-id] [--all-archived] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

delete a run's record (or all archived)

Delete a flow run's record from disk (its journal, events, and logs). This is
permanent; the run's tasks are ordinary tasks and are not touched. Pass
--all-archived to delete every archived run at once. A running run must be
stopped first.

- `<run-id>` the run to delete
- `--all-archived` delete every archived run
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory (default: current)
